newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seen ending cereals penalty set-aside.
newsitem.headline: EU seen ending cereals penalty set-aside.

text.p: European Union farm ministers may scrap next week penalties forcing farmers to take more land out of production if they exceed cereals and oilseed planting limits, EU member state officials said.
"A solution is possible," a Dutch EU Presidency official said, noting that the so-called extraordinary set-aside scheme had not been applied this season.
However farmers would still suffer financial penalties for over-planting.
An eventual agreement on extraordinary set-aside would form part of bargaining by EU farm ministers in the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price talks in Luxembourg from June 23-25.
But European Commission officials said the 1998 rate for compulsory set-aside could not be fixed next week as no proposal had been presented. The current rate is five percent.

Ministers have been deadlocked for the past year over a European Commission proposal to make penalties for overplanting Germany, France and Italy have argued that Commission plans to allow member states to target penalties on regions which over-planted did not go far enough. A series of other countries also demanded changes.
But the Commission has rejected their demands saying they would weaken efforts to curb production, cost money, infringe free trade rules and make the set-aside system too complex.
However there is general agreement on related provisions exempting drought-hit farmers in Spain from penalties.
